scenes.heading: Adaptations
scenes.sub: How life survives the driest inhabited continent
scenes.say: Australia is the driest inhabited continent, with deserts, bushfires and alpine snow. So how do our plants and animals survive here?

scenes.heading: What is an adaptation?
points: A suntan is acclimatisation, not adaptation
scenes.say: An adaptation is an inherited feature that helps an organism survive and reproduce. Adaptations build up over many generations by natural selection. A suntan isn't an adaptation. It happens in one lifetime and isn't passed on. That's called acclimatisation.

scenes.heading: Think of it like this
scenes.everyday: A footy team needs bodies, fitness and a game plan
scenes.breaks: Players train and plan in their own lives. Adaptations are inherited and built over many generations.
scenes.say: Think of a footy team playing on a hot day. Players' bodies are like structural adaptations. How their bodies handle heat inside is physiological. Their game plan, like resting in the shade, is behavioural. But players learn and plan. Adaptations are inherited, not chosen.

scenes.heading: Structural vs physiological
scenes.say: Ask yourself: is it a body part, a body process, or an action? Structural adaptations are body parts, like waxy eucalypt leaves or epicormic buds that resprout after fire. Physiological adaptations are processes inside, like a desert mouse's kidneys making very concentrated urine.

scenes.heading: Behavioural adaptations
points: Kangaroos lick their forearms to cool
Some frogs burrow in dry times
scenes.say: Behavioural adaptations are things an organism does. Kangaroos lick their forearms, and as the saliva evaporates it cools the blood. Bilbies are active at night and shelter in burrows. Lizards bask in the morning, then retreat to the shade.

scenes.heading: Classify the kangaroo
scenes.question: Classify each red kangaroo feature: elastic hind-leg tendons, embryonic diapause, licking its forearms.
lines: Answer: one kangaroo, all three types
scenes.say: Try this one. A red kangaroo's elastic hind-leg tendons are a body part, so they're structural. Embryonic diapause, pausing an embryo's development in drought, is a body process, so it's physiological. Licking its forearms is an action, so it's behavioural. One kangaroo, all three types.

scenes.heading: Surface area to volume
points: Big ears, thin limbs: high SA:V
scenes.say: Spread hot chips out and they cool fast. Pile them up and they stay warm. Animals work the same way. Big ears and long, thin limbs raise the surface area to volume ratio, losing heat in hot places. Compact bodies keep heat in.

Quick recap. Adaptations are inherited and shaped by natural selection. Structural means a body part, physiological means a body process, and behavioural means an action. In your answers, name it, classify it, and explain how it helps survival. Now try the practice questions!
